patch.sql:
with items as (
    select
        order_key,
        count(*) as item_count,
        sum(extended_price) as gross_revenue,
        sum(net_revenue) as net_revenue
    from {{ ref('fct_order_items') }}
    group by order_key
)

select
    o.order_key,
    o.customer_key,
    c.region_name,
    o.order_status,
    o.order_date,
    o.priority,
    coalesce(i.item_count, 0) as item_count,
    coalesce(i.gross_revenue, 0) as gross_revenue,
    coalesce(i.net_revenue, 0) as net_revenue,
    o.loaded_at
from {{ ref('stg_orders') }} o
left join {{ ref('dim_customers') }} c on o.customer_key = c.customer_key
left join items i on o.order_key = i.order_key
patch.explanation: The duplicate `order_key` rows were caused by the `items` CTE grouping by both `order_key` and `line_number`, which produced one row per line item. By grouping only on `order_key`, we correctly aggregate item metrics per order, ensuring a single row per order when joining back to `stg_orders`. This resolves the unique constraint failure on `order_key` without altering column names or types.

        count(*) as item_count,
        sum(extended_price) as gross_revenue,
        sum(net_revenue) as net_revenue

    group by order_key, line_number

select
    o.order_key,
    o.customer_key,
    c.region_name,
    o.order_status,
    o.order_date,
    o.priority,
    coalesce(i.item_count, 0) as item_count,
    coalesce(i.gross_revenue, 0) as gross_revenue,
    coalesce(i.net_revenue, 0) as net_revenue,
    o.loaded_at
from {{ ref('stg_orders') }} o
left join {{ ref('dim_customers') }} c on o.customer_key = c.customer_key
left join items i on o.order_key = i.order_key

output.evidence: staging.stg_orders has 15k rows, but marts.fct_orders has 60,175 rows (4x). Duplicate check shows 12,900 duplicate order_key rows. fct_order_items also 60,175 rows, indicating fct_orders joins orders to order_items without aggregation, inflating rows and causing duplicate order_key. The issue originates in the fct_orders model's join logic.

output.explanation: The duplicate `order_key` rows were caused by the `items` CTE grouping by both `order_key` and `line_number`, which produced one row per line item. By grouping only on `order_key`, we correctly aggregate item metrics per order, ensuring a single row per order when joining back to `stg_orders`. This resolves the unique constraint failure on `order_key` without altering column names or types.
